track.title: Smart Citizen India
track.tagline: 200 everyday problems: your human edge + how AI helps

lessons.title: Potholes: stay safe and get them fixed
lessons.summary: Potholes injure and kill riders every monsoon. Ride defensively and report them.

sections.b: Potholes hide under rainwater, throw two-wheelers off balance and damage vehicles. Many fatal crashes happen at night or in rain on familiar roads.

Slow down on wet or unfamiliar stretches; treat every puddle as a possible pothole. Keep both hands on the handlebar, avoid sudden braking inside a pothole, keep a safe gap so you can see the road ahead, and use your local knowledge of 'bad stretches'.

Navigation apps let users report hazards; some cities use AI dashcam and satellite analysis to map potholes automatically. Photograph the pothole with location (GPS-tagged) and post it on your city's grievance app or social handle.

Report on your municipal app (e.g. MCD 311 in Delhi), state portals or CPGRAMS (pgportal.gov.in). Courts in several states have held civic bodies responsible for pothole deaths and ordered compensation.

lessons.action: Note two dangerous potholes on your route and report one today with a photo and location.

lessons.title: Two-wheeler safety
lessons.summary: Most road deaths in India involve two-wheelers. A few habits save lives.

sections.b: Riders face trucks, potholes, rain and poor lighting. Head injuries are the leading cause of death in two-wheeler crashes.

Wear a properly fastened ISI-marked helmet every time, including on short trips, and make pillion riders wear one too. Ride defensively: assume others haven't seen you, avoid blind spots of trucks and buses, and keep lights on.
Apps can track riding behaviour and warn about speed; some helmets and phones have crash detection that alerts emergency contacts. Use navigation voice prompts instead of looking at the phone.
Helmets are mandatory for rider and pillion under the Motor Vehicles Act; helmets must meet BIS standards (ISI mark). Emergency: 112, ambulance 108.

lessons.action: Check your helmet: ISI mark, chin strap working, no cracks. Replace it if it has taken a hard hit.

lessons.title: Helping a road accident victim
lessons.summary: The first hour can save a life, and the law protects helpers.

sections.b: Bystanders often hesitate to help crash victims because they fear police harassment or legal trouble, wasting the crucial 'golden hour'.

Call 112/108 immediately, keep the scene safe (hazard lights, warn traffic), don't give water to an unconscious person, apply pressure on heavy bleeding, and don't move someone with a suspected neck injury unless there's danger. Your calm action matters most.
Phones share live location with emergency services; crash detection on some phones calls for help automatically. Maps show the nearest hospital.

Good Samaritan protections (Section 134A of the Motor Vehicles Act) protect helpers from civil or criminal liability; hospitals can't demand payment or details before treatment. A cashless treatment scheme for road accident victims was notified by the Centre in 2025.

lessons.action: Save 112 and 108 on speed dial and learn how to apply pressure to stop bleeding.

lessons.title: Wrong-side driving and lane chaos
lessons.summary: Shortcuts against traffic cause head-on crashes.

sections.b: Vehicles driving on the wrong side to save a U-turn, lane cutting and sudden merges cause many urban and highway crashes.
Never take the wrong-side shortcut, even for 200 metres. Expect wrong-side riders at service roads and night; use horn and lights sparingly but clearly, and keep extra distance at junctions.
Traffic police increasingly use AI cameras (ANPR) to detect wrong-side driving and issue e-challans automatically. Dashcams record evidence if a crash happens.
Wrong-side and dangerous driving attract fines and licence suspension under the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019. Report repeat danger spots to traffic police social handles.

lessons.action: Identify one wrong-side shortcut people use on your route and plan the legal alternative.

lessons.title: Beating traffic jams
lessons.summary: Hours lost in traffic hurt health, money and family time.

sections.b: Indian metros have some of the world's worst congestion; commuters lose many hours each week stuck in traffic.

Plan departures 20-30 minutes earlier or later than peak, combine errands, negotiate flexible hours with your employer, and use metro or carpools where possible. Use commute time for audio learning (like Gyaanly!).
Navigation apps predict traffic using millions of phones; set 'arrive by' reminders. Some cities use AI traffic signals. Carpool apps match co-workers on similar routes.
Many employers now offer hybrid work; ask HR for flexible timings. Public transport passes and metro cards reduce cost.

lessons.action: Check your commute at 3 different times this week and choose the least congested slot.

lessons.title: Auto and taxi overcharging
lessons.summary: Refused meters and inflated fares are daily frustrations.

sections.b: Auto-rickshaw drivers sometimes refuse the meter or demand extra, especially for tourists, late nights or short trips.
Agree the fare before starting if there's no meter, know approximate fares for your regular routes, stay polite but firm, and walk away if unreasonable. Small courtesy often gets a fairer deal.
Ride-hailing apps show estimated fares upfront; map apps estimate distance so you know a fair price. Share live trip details with family at night.
Many cities have transport department helplines and WhatsApp numbers for meter refusal; note the vehicle number. In emergencies call 112.

lessons.action: Note the fair fare for your two most common auto routes using a map distance estimate.

lessons.title: Walking safely without footpaths
lessons.summary: Pedestrians are among the most vulnerable road users.

sections.b: Broken or encroached footpaths force people to walk on roads; crossings are scarce and drivers rarely stop.

Walk facing oncoming traffic where there's no footpath, wear light colours or reflective strips at night, cross at signals or in groups, make eye contact with drivers, and never cross while on the phone.
Map apps show pedestrian routes and foot over-bridges; some cities let you report encroached footpaths with geotagged photos.
Pedestrians have right of way at zebra crossings. Encroachments can be reported to the municipal corporation or via CPGRAMS.

lessons.action: Plan the safest crossing point on your daily walking route.

options: In the middle of the road

lessons.title: E-challans and fake challan scams
lessons.summary: Check fines only on official sites; scammers send fake links.

sections.b: Traffic cameras issue e-challans automatically. Scammers exploit this by sending SMS links to fake payment sites that steal card details.
Never pay via SMS links. Check challans yourself on the official site, compare vehicle number and photo evidence, and dispute errors calmly with proof.
Official portals and the mParivahan app show challans with photo evidence. AI cameras reduce corruption but make errors, so always verify.
Check and pay only at echallan.parivahan.gov.in or your state police site. Report scam SMS on Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu) and cyber fraud at 1930.

lessons.action: Check your vehicle for pending challans on the official portal (not via any SMS link).

quiz.q: A challan SMS with a payment link should be…
options: Verified on the official portal first

lessons.title: Licence and vehicle papers
lessons.summary: Avoid touts; most services are online now.

sections.b: People pay touts to get driving licences, renewals or vehicle transfers done, risking fraud and fake documents.
Do it yourself step by step; keep digital copies; renew on time; learn the actual rules rather than paying for shortcuts. Honest paperwork protects you later in insurance claims.
Parivahan Sewa offers online learner licence tests, renewals and RC services; DigiLocker and mParivahan store valid digital licences and RCs.
Digital documents in DigiLocker/mParivahan are legally valid for traffic checks. Insurance and PUC certificates must be current.

lessons.action: Upload your licence and RC to DigiLocker today and note renewal dates in your calendar.

lessons.title: Driving through waterlogged roads
lessons.summary: Floodwater can stall engines and hide open drains.

sections.b: Monsoon waterlogging hides open manholes and drains, can short-circuit electric poles and floods engines.
Avoid driving or walking through unknown water; if you must, go slowly in first gear without stopping. Stay away from electric poles and wires. Never try to restart a stalled engine in water.
Weather and traffic apps show waterlogging alerts; city disaster apps and social media handles post closures. IMD alerts warn of heavy rain.
Check motor insurance for engine-protection cover. Call 112 for emergencies; report open manholes to the municipal body.

lessons.action: Check whether your vehicle insurance has engine-protect cover before the monsoon.

lessons.title: Fog driving in winter
lessons.summary: North India's winter fog causes deadly pile-ups.

sections.b: Dense fog in Delhi-NCR, Punjab, UP and Haryana reduces visibility to a few metres, causing multi-vehicle crashes on expressways.

Slow down drastically, use low-beam headlights and fog lamps (not high beam), follow lane markings, keep big gaps and avoid overtaking. If visibility is near zero, stop safely away from the road with hazard lights.
IMD and traffic apps issue fog alerts; postpone non-urgent travel. Some expressways use smart display boards for speed advice.
Expressway authorities often reduce speed limits in fog. Emergency: 112. NHAI helpline: 1033.

lessons.action: Check your fog lamps and hazard lights work before winter.

options: Stop safely off the road with hazards on

lessons.title: Stray cattle on roads
lessons.summary: Cattle on highways cause sudden, serious crashes.

sections.b: Stray cattle sit on highways and city roads, especially at night, causing collisions.
Slow down near villages and markets, watch for eyes reflecting in headlights, don't swerve violently, and honk gently. Local knowledge of risky stretches helps.
Some cities use GPS-tagged complaint apps for stray cattle; reflective collars on cattle are being tried in several states.
Report stray cattle hotspots to the municipal or district administration; NHAI helpline 1033 on highways.

lessons.action: Mark two stretches on your route where cattle often appear and slow down there.

lessons.title: Night travel and drunk driving
lessons.summary: Night hours carry higher crash risk.

sections.b: Drunk drivers, tired truckers and poor lighting make late-night travel risky.
Never drive after drinking; use a cab or designated driver. Avoid driving between 1-5 am when fatigue peaks. Take a break every two hours on long trips.
Ride apps, designated-driver services and fatigue alerts in newer cars help. Share live location with family.
Drunk driving penalties under the 2019 MV Amendment are heavy (fines and possible jail). Emergency: 112.

lessons.action: Save a ride-hailing app and one trusted driver's number for nights you shouldn't drive.

quiz.q: On long drives take a break every…

options: Use a cab or designated driver

lessons.title: Safe school transport
lessons.summary: Overloaded vans and autos put children at risk.

sections.b: Many children travel in overcrowded vans or autos without seats, belts or verified drivers.
Visit the vehicle, count seats, check the driver's licence and police verification, and talk to other parents. Teach children to share if something feels unsafe.
GPS tracking apps for school buses let parents track live location; schools can share driver details digitally.
School bus safety guidelines (based on Supreme Court directions) require speed governors, first-aid kits, attendants and verified drivers. Child helpline: 1098.

lessons.action: Check your child's school transport: seats, belts, driver verification, and emergency contacts.

lessons.title: Parking disputes and towing
lessons.summary: Parking fights escalate quickly; know rules and stay calm.

sections.b: Limited parking leads to fights with neighbours, illegal parking fines and towing.
Use designated parking, respect gates and driveways, keep a note with your phone number on the dashboard, and stay calm in disputes. De-escalation prevents violence.
Parking apps show available spots and paid parking; some cities have smart parking systems.
Towing must follow official procedure with a receipt; vehicles are taken to designated yards. Check your city traffic police site for towed vehicles.

lessons.action: Put a polite contact note on your dashboard and check your society's parking rules.

options: Leaving a contact note on the dashboard

lessons.title: FASTag and toll problems
lessons.summary: Double deductions and blacklisted tags cause delays and fines.

sections.b: FASTag issues include double deductions, blacklisting due to low balance or incomplete KYC, and paying double toll when the tag fails.
Keep enough balance, complete KYC, check SMS alerts after each toll and dispute wrong deductions quickly with screenshots.
Bank/issuer apps show transaction history; AI-based number-plate tolling is being piloted on some highways.
Raise disputes with your FASTag issuer bank; NHAI helpline 1033. Keep one tag per vehicle.

lessons.action: Check your FASTag KYC status and last 5 transactions today.

lessons.title: Crowded trains and pickpockets
lessons.summary: Rush hour brings theft and safety risks.

sections.b: Packed metros, local trains and buses enable pickpocketing, harassment and dangerous door-hanging.

Keep phones and wallets in front pockets or zipped bags, avoid standing at doors, travel in women's coaches when needed, and step away from anyone making you uncomfortable. Speak up; others often support you.
Metro apps show crowd levels at some stations; phone 'find my device' and CEIR blocking help recover stolen phones.
Railway helpline 139 (RailMadad); metro security helplines; women's helpline 181; emergency 112. Block stolen phones on Sanchar Saathi (CEIR).

lessons.action: Enable 'Find my device' on your phone and note your IMEI number (dial *#06#).

lessons.title: Train travel complaints
lessons.summary: Dirty coaches, AC failures or harassment: complain effectively.

sections.b: Passengers face unclean coaches, broken AC, overcharging by vendors and safety concerns on long trips.
Complain politely with specifics (train number, coach, berth), document with photos, and help fellow passengers raise issues together.
RailMadad app/website routes complaints to the right team, often while you're still on the train; PNR and coach details auto-fill.
RailMadad: 139 or railmadad.indianrail.gov.in. Vendors must charge printed prices (MRP).

lessons.action: Install or bookmark RailMadad before your next train journey.

options: Train number, coach, berth and photos

lessons.title: Highway fatigue and unmarked speed breakers
lessons.summary: Long drives and hidden breakers cause crashes.

sections.b: Unmarked speed breakers, sudden diversions and driver fatigue cause many highway crashes.
Plan rest stops, avoid driving more than 8-10 hours a day, share driving, watch for villages and markets (breakers likely), and slow down where the road narrows.
Navigation apps announce some speed breakers and hazards; newer cars warn of drowsiness and lane drift.
NHAI helpline 1033 for highway emergencies and hazards; report dangerous breakers to authorities.

lessons.action: Before your next long drive, plan two rest stops on the map.

lessons.title: Seat belts and child seats
lessons.summary: Rear-seat belts and child seats save lives.

sections.b: Many people skip seat belts in the rear seat and carry children on laps, which is deadly in a crash.
Everyone buckles up, front and rear. Use proper child seats for young children, never hold a child on your lap in a moving car, and lead by example.
Cars now beep for rear belts too; safety ratings (Bharat NCAP) help choose safer cars.
Rear seat belts are mandatory under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules. Bharat NCAP gives star safety ratings for cars.

lessons.action: Make 'everyone buckled before we move' a family rule from today.

lessons.title: Reading the AQI correctly
lessons.summary: Know what the air quality number means for your day.

sections.b: NCR and many Indian cities hit 'Very Poor' or 'Severe' AQI in winter. Many people ignore it or misread it.

Check AQI before outdoor plans, especially for children, elders and anyone with asthma or heart issues. Shift exercise indoors on bad days and keep windows closed during peak pollution (early morning and late night in winter).
Apps like SAMEER (CPCB) show station-wise AQI; AI forecasts predict next-day air quality so you can plan.
India's AQI bands: Good 0-50, Satisfactory 51-100, Moderate 101-200, Poor 201-300, Very Poor 301-400, Severe 401-500.

lessons.action: Install SAMEER or another AQI app and check your area's AQI each morning this week.

lessons.title: Choosing and wearing a mask
lessons.summary: Cloth masks don't stop fine particles. Use N95/N99 properly.

sections.b: PM2.5 particles go deep into lungs. Cloth and surgical masks offer little protection against them.
Use a well-fitting N95/N99 or equivalent (FFP2) mask, press the nose clip, check for air leaks, and replace when breathing gets hard or it's dirty. Fit matters more than brand.
AQI apps tell you when masks are needed; some masks carry certification codes you can verify online.
Look for genuine certifications (e.g. BIS IS 9473 for respirators, or NIOSH N95). Children need properly sized masks.

lessons.action: Do a fit check: wear your mask and breathe out hard; if air leaks around the edges, adjust or change it.

lessons.title: Cleaner indoor air
lessons.summary: Indoor air can be as polluted as outside unless you act.

sections.b: Smog enters homes; cooking smoke, incense and mosquito coils add more pollution indoors.

Keep windows shut at peak pollution hours and ventilate when AQI improves (often afternoon). Use exhaust fans while cooking, avoid incense and coils indoors on bad days, and wet-mop instead of sweeping dust.
Air purifiers with HEPA filters reduce PM2.5 in a closed room; low-cost sensors show indoor AQI so you know if it's working.
Choose purifiers by CADR (clean air delivery rate) suited to your room size. Plants alone don't clean air meaningfully.

lessons.action: If you have a purifier, run it in the bedroom with doors closed tonight; otherwise wet-mop and close windows at night.

lessons.title: Stubble season and GRAP
lessons.summary: Know what changes when pollution emergency stages kick in.

sections.b: From October to January, stubble burning, vehicle emissions, dust and low winds push NCR's AQI to severe levels.
Plan ahead: work from home if possible on severe days, avoid long outdoor exposure, check school advisories and support farmers' alternatives to burning.
Satellites detect farm fires daily; AI models forecast pollution episodes, helping authorities trigger action earlier.
The Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) has stages that restrict construction, certain vehicles and activities as AQI worsens; the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) issues orders.

lessons.action: Check the current GRAP stage for NCR and what it restricts.

lessons.title: Exercising in polluted cities
lessons.summary: Exercise is healthy, but timing and place matter.

sections.b: During exercise you breathe much more air, so in high pollution you inhale more particles.
On poor AQI days, exercise indoors, choose parks away from traffic, avoid early-morning winter smog and reduce intensity. Keep fitness going rather than stopping altogether.
AQI forecast apps help pick cleaner hours; fitness apps offer indoor workouts.
People with asthma or heart conditions should follow doctor advice on bad air days.

lessons.action: Plan two indoor workouts for this week's worst AQI days.

options: You breathe more air and particles

lessons.title: Protecting children and elders from smog
lessons.summary: Young lungs and older hearts are most at risk.

sections.b: Children breathe faster and are closer to vehicle exhaust; elders with heart or lung disease face higher risks during smog.
Limit outdoor play on bad days, use properly sized masks, keep inhalers ready, watch for breathlessness or chest pain, and keep bedrooms as the cleanest room.
AQI alerts, school advisories and purifier sensors help decide daily routines.
Schools may shift timings or go online under GRAP. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty; emergency 112.

lessons.action: Make a 'bad air day plan' for your family: indoor activities, mask sizes, medicines.

quiz.q: Why are children more vulnerable to smog?
options: They breathe faster and are closer to exhaust

lessons.title: Firecrackers and festival air
lessons.summary: Celebrate without poisoning your neighbourhood.

sections.b: Firecrackers spike PM2.5 and noise for days, hurting asthmatics, pets and elders, and causing burns.
Celebrate with lights, rangoli, food and community gatherings; if crackers are allowed, use green crackers in permitted hours and keep water/sand nearby.
Apps show permitted timings and AQI; community groups organise cracker-free celebrations.
Courts and states often restrict crackers in NCR; check local rules. Burns: cool with running water, don't apply toothpaste; call 112 for serious injuries.

lessons.action: Plan a cracker-free festival activity with family or neighbours.

lessons.title: Construction dust
lessons.summary: Uncovered construction and roadside dust add heavily to PM10.

sections.b: Open construction sites, debris and unpaved roads throw dust into the air, especially in dry seasons.
Report violations with photos, keep windows closed near active sites, and in your own renovations cover materials and sprinkle water.
Some cities use AI cameras and drones to detect dust violations; complaint apps accept geotagged photos.
Dust control norms require covering, water sprinkling and anti-smog guns at large sites. In Delhi, the Green Delhi app takes pollution complaints.

lessons.action: If you see an uncovered site, report it with a photo and location on your city's pollution complaint app.

lessons.title: Open garbage burning
lessons.summary: Burning waste releases toxic smoke into homes.

sections.b: Garbage and leaf burning, common in winter for warmth, releases toxic smoke including dioxins from plastic.
Never burn waste; talk to neighbours and guards about the harm (and offer alternatives like composting leaves). Report repeated burning politely but firmly.
Complaint apps accept photos; satellite and camera systems detect fires in some cities.
Open burning of waste is banned under Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 and NGT orders; fines apply.

lessons.action: Ask your society guards how they stay warm in winter; suggest safe heaters instead of burning waste.

lessons.title: Is your drinking water safe?
lessons.summary: Contaminated water causes typhoid, jaundice and diarrhoea.

sections.b: Old pipelines, leaks next to sewer lines and storage tanks can contaminate tap water, especially in monsoon.
Watch for smell, colour or taste changes; clean storage tanks every 6 months; boil water during outbreaks; keep drinking water covered and use a ladle instead of dipping glasses.
Home test kits check TDS, pH and bacteria; some water boards share quality data online. Smart purifiers alert when filters need changing.
Drinking water standard in India is BIS IS 10500. Complain to your water utility about dirty supply; outbreaks can be reported to local health authorities.

lessons.action: Check when your water tank was last cleaned and schedule a cleaning.

lessons.title: RO purifiers: when you need one
lessons.summary: RO isn't always necessary, and it wastes water.

sections.b: Many homes use RO purifiers even with low-TDS municipal water, wasting a lot of water and removing useful minerals.
Test your water TDS: if TDS is low and the issue is germs, UV/UF may be enough. If TDS is high or there's fluoride/arsenic, RO helps. Reuse RO reject water for mopping or plants (if not too salty).
TDS meters are cheap; smart purifiers monitor quality and filter life.
The NGT has raised concerns about RO water wastage where TDS is low. Follow BIS IS 10500 limits for TDS (acceptable up to 500 mg/L).

lessons.action: Measure your tap water TDS with a meter (or ask a purifier technician) and decide what treatment you really need.

lessons.title: Groundwater: fluoride, arsenic and nitrates
lessons.summary: Borewell water can carry invisible poisons.

sections.b: In parts of India, groundwater contains excess fluoride, arsenic, nitrate or iron, causing bone, skin and organ damage over years.
Get borewell water tested in a certified lab before drinking. Use appropriate treatment (RO, community purification plants), and check with neighbours about local water history.
Government data dashboards (Jal Shakti/CGWB) map contamination areas; labs share digital reports.
Water testing is available at NABL-accredited labs and district water testing labs under Jal Jeevan Mission.

lessons.action: Find the nearest district or NABL-accredited water testing lab.

lessons.title: Water shortages and tankers
lessons.summary: Summer shortages push families to costly, unreliable tankers.

sections.b: Many cities face summer water shortages; private tankers charge high prices and quality is uncertain.
Store water safely, fix leaks, reuse water from washing vegetables for plants, and coordinate with neighbours for shared tankers from authorised suppliers.
Water utility apps book official tankers in some cities; smart meters detect leaks.
Many water boards run official tanker booking (e.g. Delhi Jal Board). Complain about irregular supply to your utility.

lessons.action: Check your home for leaking taps or toilets (a dripping tap can waste thousands of litres a year).

lessons.title: Stored water and mosquitoes
lessons.summary: Clean stored water breeds dengue mosquitoes.

sections.b: Aedes mosquitoes, which spread dengue and chikungunya, breed in clean stagnant water in buckets, coolers, plant trays and tyres.
Empty and scrub containers weekly ('dry day'), cover water tanks, clean cooler water, and check rooftops for old tyres or pots.
City health departments use drones and apps to track breeding; reminders help you keep a weekly dry day.
Municipal bodies can fine households for mosquito breeding during outbreaks. Report breeding sites to the local health department.

lessons.action: Do a 10-minute 'mosquito check' of your home and roof today.

lessons.title: Polluted rivers like the Yamuna
lessons.summary: What citizens can do about toxic foam and sewage.

sections.b: Untreated sewage and industrial waste pollute rivers, causing toxic foam and killing aquatic life.
Don't dump waste or puja material into rivers (use designated kunds), avoid phosphate-heavy detergents, and support local clean-up and monitoring groups.
Satellite and sensor data track river quality; citizen science apps record pollution sightings.
Report polluting industries to the State Pollution Control Board or CPCB; NGT hears environmental cases.

lessons.action: Use a phosphate-free detergent and dispose of puja waste at designated points.

lessons.title: Noise: honking and loudspeakers
lessons.summary: Constant noise harms sleep, hearing and heart health.

sections.b: Honking, loudspeakers, construction and generators keep noise levels high, especially at night.
Honk only when necessary, talk to neighbours or organisers politely first, use earplugs for sleep, and report persistent violations.
Phone apps measure decibels so you can document noise; some cities use acoustic cameras to catch honkers.
Noise Pollution Rules, 2000 restrict loudspeakers between 10 pm and 6 am (with limited exceptions) and set zone limits. Complain to police (112) for late-night violations.

lessons.action: Use a decibel app to measure noise at your window at night once this week.

lessons.title: Plastic waste
lessons.summary: Single-use plastic clogs drains and causes floods.

sections.b: Plastic bags and wrappers block drains, worsen urban flooding and harm cattle that eat them.
Carry a cloth bag and bottle, refuse straws and extra packaging, segregate plastic for recycling and support shops that avoid plastic.
Recycling apps and kabadiwala platforms pick up segregated dry waste; some pay for it.
Several single-use plastic items have been banned nationally since July 2022. Complain about violations to the municipal body or pollution control board.

lessons.action: Keep a cloth bag in your bag or vehicle starting today.

lessons.title: E-waste disposal
lessons.summary: Old phones and batteries leak toxins if dumped.

sections.b: Old phones, chargers, batteries and appliances contain lead, mercury and lithium that harm soil and workers in informal recycling.
Store e-waste separately, wipe data from devices, and give them to authorised recyclers or brand take-back programmes, not regular garbage.
Brand apps and recycler websites schedule pickups; data-wipe tools protect your privacy.
E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 make producers responsible for collection; look for CPCB-authorised recyclers.

lessons.action: Collect old chargers, batteries and phones at home into one box for authorised recycling.

quiz.q: Before recycling a phone you should…

lessons.title: Urban heat at home
lessons.summary: Concrete cities trap heat; homes become ovens in summer.

sections.b: Heat islands make cities several degrees hotter than surroundings, and tin or concrete roofs make homes unbearable.
Paint roofs white/reflective (cool roofs), use curtains on sun-facing windows, cross-ventilate at night, plant trees and use shaded balconies. Help elderly neighbours during heatwaves.
Weather apps give heat alerts; smart plugs and timers run fans/coolers efficiently.
Several cities have Heat Action Plans (pioneered by Ahmedabad). IMD issues heatwave warnings.

Make a plan: meeting points, out-of-town contact, important documents, medicines and a ready bag. Practise once a year.
Phones store emergency info; family location sharing helps reunite.
NDMA guidelines for family preparedness; emergency 112.

lessons.action: Agree on a family meeting point and an out-of-town contact this week.

lessons.title: Winter heaters and carbon monoxide
lessons.summary: Closed rooms with angithis can kill silently.

sections.b: In North Indian winters, people sleep with coal angithis or gas heaters in closed rooms, causing carbon monoxide poisoning.
Never sleep with coal or gas heaters burning in a closed room; ventilate; use electric heaters with care; know symptoms: headache, dizziness, nausea.
CO detectors alert early; weather apps warn of cold waves.
Emergency 108/112; move affected people to fresh air immediately.

lessons.action: Warn your family and guards never to sleep with an angithi burning indoors.

quiz.q: Carbon monoxide is dangerous because it is…

options: Move the person to fresh air and call 108

lessons.title: Milk adulteration
lessons.summary: Simple home tests can reveal watered or adulterated milk.

sections.b: Milk is sometimes diluted with water or adulterated with detergent or starch.
Buy from trusted sources, check packaging and FSSAI licence, and try simple tests: a drop of pure milk on a slanted surface flows slowly leaving a trail; watered milk flows fast without a trail.
FSSAI's DART book lists quick home tests; apps verify FSSAI licences.
Report adulteration to the FSSAI Food Safety Connect app or helpline 1800-11-2100.

lessons.action: Try the slanted-surface drop test on your milk this week.

quiz.q: FSSAI's guide for home adulteration tests is…
Watered milk on a slanted surface…

lessons.title: Adulterated spices and oils
lessons.summary: Colour and cheap fillers can hide harmful additives.

sections.b: Spices may contain artificial colours, brick powder or sawdust; oils may be mixed with cheaper oils.
Buy sealed, reputed brands with FSSAI licence; try simple tests (e.g. turmeric in water, artificial colour leaves streaks); avoid unusually bright loose spices.
FSSAI's DART booklet and videos show quick tests; licence verification online.
Complain through Food Safety Connect; FSSAI licence numbers are printed on packs.

lessons.action: Check the FSSAI licence number on two packaged food items at home.

quiz.q: Unusually bright loose spices may indicate…

lessons.title: Pesticides on fruits and vegetables
lessons.summary: Wash smart to reduce residues.

sections.b: Fruits and vegetables can carry pesticide residues and wax coatings.
Wash under running water, soak in salt water (2%) for a few minutes, peel where appropriate, and buy seasonal and local produce.
Apps and labels for certified organic (Jaivik Bharat) produce help; some kits test residues.
Look for 'Jaivik Bharat' logo for certified organic food; report issues to FSSAI.

lessons.action: Wash this week's vegetables with a short salt-water soak followed by running water.

quiz.q: Certified organic food in India carries…

lessons.title: MRP overcharging and expired goods
lessons.summary: You never have to pay more than MRP.

sections.b: Shops charge above MRP (especially for cold drinks, water at tourist spots) or sell expired items.
Check MRP and expiry before paying, ask for bills, and refuse overcharges politely; report persistent violators.
Consumer helpline app takes complaints with photos; scan barcodes to check product details.
Selling above MRP violates Legal Metrology rules; complain to the National Consumer Helpline (1915) or the state Legal Metrology department.

lessons.action: Check expiry dates on items in your fridge and pantry today.

options: A violation of Legal Metrology rules

lessons.title: Reading food labels
lessons.summary: Hidden sugar and salt are everywhere.

sections.b: Packaged foods market themselves as 'healthy' while containing high sugar, salt or trans fat.
Read the ingredient list (first items are largest), check sugar, sodium and saturated fat per serving, and compare brands.
Label-scanning apps rate products; AI can explain nutrition labels.
FSSAI regulates labelling; trans fat limits apply to fats and oils.

lessons.action: Compare sugar per 100 g in two breakfast cereals or biscuits at home.

quiz.q: A hidden health risk in packaged food is…

lessons.title: Restaurant service charges
lessons.summary: Service charge is voluntary.

sections.b: Restaurants add 'service charge' automatically to bills.
Check the bill; you can ask for it to be removed and tip voluntarily if you wish. Stay polite.
Consumer helpline app takes complaints with bill photos.
CCPA guidelines (2022) say restaurants can't add service charge automatically or by default; complain at 1915.

lessons.action: Next time you eat out, check the bill for an automatic service charge.

quiz.q: If added by default you can…

lessons.title: Online delivery problems
lessons.summary: Wrong items, missing refunds and fake deliveries.

sections.b: Customers face wrong products, delayed refunds and 'delivered' items that never arrived.
Record unboxing videos for expensive items, report issues quickly in-app, keep screenshots, and escalate via grievance officers.
In-app chat and AI support resolve many issues; order tracking shows delivery evidence.
E-commerce rules require platforms to have grievance officers; National Consumer Helpline 1915; e-Daakhil for disputes.

lessons.action: Record an unboxing video for your next expensive online order.

lessons.title: Fake reviews and dark patterns
lessons.summary: Designs that trick you into buying.

sections.b: Fake reviews, false urgency ('only 1 left!'), hidden charges and hard-to-cancel subscriptions manipulate shoppers.
Read critical reviews, ignore countdown pressure, check the final price before paying, and avoid pre-ticked add-ons.
Review analysis tools spot fake patterns; AI can summarise genuine reviews.
CCPA's Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 ban practices like false urgency, basket sneaking and subscription traps; complain at 1915.

lessons.action: Next time you shop online, check the final checkout amount for added items you didn't choose.

quiz.q: A countdown timer saying 'offer ends in 2 minutes' is often…

lessons.title: Warranties and returns
lessons.summary: Know what you're entitled to.

sections.b: Sellers refuse repairs under warranty or deny returns of defective products.
Keep invoices and warranty cards (digital copies), register products, note service request numbers, and escalate in writing.
Brand apps register warranties; AI drafts complaint emails.
Defective products can be challenged under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019; 1915 helpline; e-Daakhil.

lessons.action: Photograph invoices and warranty cards of your appliances and save them in one folder.

quiz.q: Keep which documents for warranty claims?

lessons.title: Buying gold jewellery
lessons.summary: Hallmarking protects your purity.

sections.b: Buyers get lower-purity gold than paid for or face unfair making charges.
Buy hallmarked jewellery, check the 6-digit HUID, ask for a detailed bill (weight, purity, making charges), and compare stores.
BIS CARE app verifies HUID and purity details.
Hallmarking with HUID is mandatory for most gold jewellery sales; verify on the BIS CARE app.

lessons.action: If you own hallmarked jewellery, verify one piece's HUID on the BIS CARE app.

lessons.title: Mobile and internet billing
lessons.summary: Avoid surprise charges and poor service.

sections.b: Unwanted value-added services, poor network and porting hassles annoy users.
Check bills, deactivate unwanted services, compare plans, and port your number if service is poor.
Telecom apps show usage; TRAI's apps measure speed and call drops.
Port your number via SMS 'PORT <number>' to 1900; complaints to the operator's appellate authority; TRAI DND 1909.

lessons.action: Check your mobile account for any active value-added services you didn't request.

quiz.q: To port your number, SMS PORT to…

lessons.title: Flight cancellations and refunds
lessons.summary: Know airline obligations.

sections.b: Passengers face cancellations, denied boarding and delayed refunds.
Keep booking details, ask for written reasons, request refunds/alternatives, and know your rights before accepting vouchers.
Airline apps rebook; AirSewa portal tracks grievances.
DGCA's Passenger Charter sets compensation and facilities for cancellations, delays and denied boarding; complain on AirSewa.

lessons.action: Bookmark AirSewa before your next flight.

quiz.q: Before accepting a voucher you should…

lessons.title: Edtech and coaching mis-selling
lessons.summary: Pressure sales and loans for courses.

sections.b: Some edtech/coaching companies push expensive courses with loans and refuse refunds.
Take a trial, read refund policies, avoid course loans under pressure, and check reviews from real students.
Course comparison sites and free alternatives (SWAYAM) help decide; AI can summarise contract terms.
Unfair practices can be reported to the National Consumer Helpline (1915) and e-Daakhil.

lessons.action: Before buying any course, find a free alternative to compare.

quiz.q: Before paying for a course you should…
options: Read refund policy and take a trial

lessons.title: Weighing scale cheating
lessons.summary: Make sure you get the quantity you pay for.

sections.b: Vendors sometimes use tampered scales or weigh items with packaging.
Watch the scale, ask for tare (zero) before weighing, check stamped verification on scales, and reweigh at home if suspicious.
Digital scales show weight clearly; complaints can be filed with photos.
Legal Metrology departments verify and stamp weighing instruments; complain to them or 1915.

lessons.action: Next time you shop, ensure the scale shows zero before your items go on.

quiz.q: Before weighing, the scale should show…

lessons.title: Healthy eating on a budget
lessons.summary: Nutrition doesn't need expensive foods.

sections.b: Rising prices push families to cheap processed foods with poor nutrition.
Base meals on dals, seasonal vegetables, millets, eggs/curd, and limit packaged snacks; plan weekly menus and buy in season.
Meal planning apps and AI suggest budget recipes using what you have.
Government nutrition programmes (POSHAN Abhiyaan, mid-day meals) support children and mothers; millets promoted for nutrition.

lessons.action: Plan one week's budget meals including millets and seasonal vegetables.

lessons.title: Plastic bottles in heat
lessons.summary: Store water safely, especially in cars.

sections.b: Bottled water stored in heat or reused single-use bottles raise hygiene and quality concerns.
Prefer steel or glass bottles, avoid leaving plastic bottles in hot cars, and check seals and BIS/ISI marks on packaged water.
Label apps verify certifications; filter bottles help when travelling.
Packaged drinking water must have BIS certification (ISI mark) and FSSAI licence.

lessons.action: Switch to a reusable steel bottle this week.

lessons.title: Subscription traps and auto-pay
lessons.summary: Small recurring charges drain money.

sections.b: Free trials convert to paid plans; UPI autopay mandates keep charging for unused services.
Review subscriptions monthly, cancel unused ones, set reminders before trials end, and check UPI autopay mandates in your app.
UPI apps list active mandates; AI budget tools flag recurring charges.
RBI rules require pre-debit notifications for recurring payments; dark-pattern guidelines target subscription traps.

lessons.action: Open your UPI app and review active autopay mandates today.

quiz.q: Active UPI autopay mandates can be checked in…
Before a free trial ends you should…
options: Decide and cancel if not needed

lessons.title: Buying second-hand phones and vehicles
lessons.summary: Avoid stolen goods and hidden problems.

sections.b: Used phones may be stolen or blacklisted; used vehicles may have loans, accidents or pending challans.
Check IMEI status, get bills/IDs from sellers; for vehicles verify RC, loan/hypothecation, insurance and challans, and transfer ownership properly.
Sanchar Saathi checks IMEI status (KYM); Parivahan/Vahan shows vehicle details.
Check device genuineness via 'Know Your Mobile' on Sanchar Saathi; complete RC transfer through Parivahan.

lessons.action: Learn how to check a phone's IMEI status on Sanchar Saathi.

quiz.q: Check a used phone's IMEI via…

lessons.title: ISI marks and product safety
lessons.summary: Certified products protect your family.

sections.b: Fake or uncertified helmets, pressure cookers, heaters and toys can injure users.
Buy ISI-marked products where mandatory, check licence numbers, and avoid suspiciously cheap safety products.
BIS CARE app verifies ISI licences and lets you complain.
Many products (helmets, pressure cookers, toys, electrical appliances) are under mandatory BIS certification.

lessons.action: Check the ISI mark on your pressure cooker or helmet using the BIS CARE app.

lessons.title: Becoming a smart citizen
lessons.summary: Combine human judgment with AI tools to solve everyday problems.

sections.b: Everyday problems in India (pollution, scams, paperwork, safety) can feel overwhelming.
Your edge is judgment, community and persistence: verify information, help neighbours, raise issues together, and keep learning. One informed citizen influences many.
AI helps you draft complaints, find schemes, understand documents and spot scams. Always verify with official sources and use AI as a helper, not an authority.
Key portals: CPGRAMS, RTI Online, cybercrime.gov.in, e-Daakhil, myScheme, DigiLocker, Sanchar Saathi; helplines 112, 1930, 1915.

lessons.action: Share three helpful portals or helplines from this path with your family group. 🇮🇳
